metadata.title: Sexual Content Reviewer Knowledge Pack
metadata.description: Full academy knowledge pack for sexual content, intimacy, framing, and exception reasoning.

pack.title: Sexual Content Reviewer Knowledge Pack
pack.purpose: Teach reviewers how to reason about sexual content, intimacy, visual framing, consent, exception handling, and implicit meaning without collapsing distinct concepts into one node.
required_evidence: Direct sexual reference or unmistakable innuendo anchored in the exact literal span.
Mutual or pressured intimacy clues when the scene is about flirtation, romance, touch, or invitation.
Scene, camera, sound, or body-language evidence when the sexual meaning is visual rather than spoken.
Context markers such as medical, educational, historical, documentary, or court settings before treating the text as a violation.
Separate harm, harassment, exploitation, and grooming from consensual romance or neutral depiction.
Recover implicit sexuality from double meaning, metaphor, symbolism, or indirect speech only when the scene supports that reading.
insufficient_evidence: A neutral mention, a wardrobe note, or a non-sexual medical term with no sexual frame.
A family affection scene that is mistaken for intimacy without corroboration.
A quoted, reported, or condemned line that the story does not endorse.
A dream, flashback, or imagination sequence with no recoverable sexual meaning.
reviewer_heuristics: Do not collapse mention, implication, depiction, and framing into one judgment.
Always separate flirting from harassment, and suggestion from coercion.
Check whether the sexual meaning comes from speech, camera language, sound, or body language.
Treat double meaning, metaphor, symbolism, and indirect speech as sexual meaning only when the context makes the reading recoverable.
Treat educational, medical, historical, documentary, and court contexts as exception-heavy.
Give the story time to explain itself before finalizing a finding.
Use the shortest literal evidence span that still proves the sexual meaning.
positive_examples: Explicit sexual reference in dialogue that is not framed as a joke or report.
A scene that clearly sexualizes the body through camera and sound cues.
An unwanted sexual advance that the target rejects.
A grooming pattern that unfolds across multiple sentences or scenes.
A false accusation that is later corrected is still a reviewable false accusation concept.
A euphemism or symbol whose sexual meaning is only recoverable from context.
negative_examples: A medical explanation in a clinic.
A history lesson about marriage customs.
A police report that repeats a quoted complaint.
A documentary description of a relevant scene without endorsement.
A figurative line with no recoverable sexual meaning.
common_false_positives: Medical terminology mistaken for erotic language.
Family warmth or friendship mistaken for intimacy.
Wardrobe or camera directions that are not sexualized.
A quotation or report treated as endorsement.
Dream or flashback content treated as present-time reality.
A false accusation treated as a real finding without confirmation.
Indirect speech treated as explicit sexual content when the scene does not support it.

glossary_relationships.note: Often signals a direct reference or hint.
Often marks flirtation or romantic pressure.
Often appears in coercive or abusive contexts.
Medical context may lower false positives.
May indicate a false accusation concept when later corrected.
Implicit sexual suggestion can be recoverable from context.
Double meaning can carry recoverable sexual intent.

article_mapping.note: Primary content-standard mapping for sexual content.
Use when content suitability or rating is implicated.
Use when the scene turns sexual language into coercive harm.
Use when the sexual content targets a child or minor.
Use for invasive framing or false sexual allegations.

reporting_guidance: Report the shortest exact evidence span that carries the sexual meaning.
State the framing explicitly: reference, flirtation, harm, documentary, medical, historical, dream, or false accusation.
If the scene is exception-heavy, say why the confidence is reduced rather than pretending the concept vanished.
Keep the report aligned with the exact concept rather than collapsing to generic sexual content.
